title: Completed pullback is left adjoint to direct image
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $I\subset A$ be an ideal. Write $D(\mathcal C,A)$ for the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] over the constant sheaf $\underline A$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $\mathcal C$, and similarly for $\mathcal D$. Let $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal C,A)$ be its full subcategory of derived $I$-complete complexes: for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every local section $a\in (I\underline A)(U)$, the derived sheaf Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] from $\underline A|_U[1/a]$ to $K|_U$ is zero. Here $\underline A|_U[1/a]$ is the sheafification of sectionwise localization, and derived sheaf Hom means the right derived functor of sheaf Hom.

Derived completion $C_{\mathcal C}:D(\mathcal C,A)\to D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal C,A)$ is left adjoint to the full inclusion; its underlying object is canonically
$$C_{\mathcal C}K=R\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(K\otimes_A^L\underline{A/I^n}).$$
Here $\otimes^L$ is the left derived functor of the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $R\varprojlim$ is computed by resolving a strict inverse sequence by a K-injective sequence complex (a complex such that every map to it from an acyclic sequence complex is null-homotopic) and then taking its inverse limit. The completion map is the unit of this adjunction.

Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with finite-limit-preserving inverse image. Use the canonical identification $u^{-1}\underline A=\underline A$ and the resulting exact inverse image of $A$-module sheaves. Let $Lu^*$ be this inverse image on derived categories and let $Ru_*$ be the K-injective total right derived direct image [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then $Ru_*$ preserves derived $I$-complete complexes and
$$L u^*_{\mathrm{comp}}:=C_{\mathcal D}\circ Lu^*|_{D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal C,A)}\ \dashv\ Ru_*|_{D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal D,A)}.$$
This is the adjunction induced by the ordinary derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunction and the completion adjunction; in particular its units and counits are fixed by those two hom-set bijections.

proof.text:
Put $F=u^{-1}$ and $G=u_*$ on constant-$A$ module sheaves. The ring identification in the statement makes the tensor-formula adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] precisely $F\dashv G$, with $F$ exact. Thus $F$ preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms, and its termwise functor descends to $Lu^*$. For a complex $N$, choose a functorial K-injective resolution $N\to J$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Since $F$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] says $GJ$ is K-injective. For every complex $M$, the termwise adjunction respects differentials and chain homotopies, giving
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal D,A)}(FM,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal D,A)}(FM,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal C,A)}(M,GJ)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal C,A)}(M,Ru_*N).$$
The two outer bijections are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. The termwise adjunction is natural, and the functorial resolution and localization preserve these naturality equations. This fixes the ordinary derived adjunction, without any boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose a finite generating list $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $I$, allowing the empty list when $I=0$. On each site apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] to $\mathcal O=\underline A$ and these global sections. Its local completeness condition is exactly the condition in the item, and its unit $\eta_K$ gives the natural reflector Hom bijection. The last paragraph of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], specialized to $\mathcal O=\underline A$, identifies this Koszul reflector with $R\lim_{n\geq1}(K\otimes^L_A\underline{A/I^n})$, respecting the unit. This proves the asserted quotient-tower model and completion map; no change of coefficient ring is needed here.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion, proof: finite generators and Koszul/quotient comparison

proof.text:
For a global scalar $a\in A$, let $X(H,a)$ be the strict tower on a representative of $H$ with every transition multiplication by $a$, and put $T(H,a)=R\lim X(H,a)$. A quasi-isomorphism of representatives gives a levelwise quasi-isomorphism of towers, so this is independent of the representative. Apply [lem-sp-slice-restriction-strict-derived-limit] to obtain, with the actual scalar transitions,
$$T(H,a)|_U\cong T(H|_U,a|_U).$$
By the Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], each total strict limit $T(H|_U,a|_U)$ is a derived limit of its tower in the sense used by [lem-weil-pbc-local-hom-tower-criterion]. By that criterion, $T(H,a)=0$ therefore implies $R\mathcal Hom_{\underline A_U}(\underline A_U[1/a],H|_U)=0$ for every $U$. Conversely, those vanishing statements make every restriction of $T(H,a)$ zero. Restriction is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so every cohomology sheaf restricts to zero. Its sections over $U$ vanish by evaluation at the terminal object $U\to U$ of the slice. All cohomology sheaves are zero, so $0\to T(H,a)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and hence invertible in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text:
Let $N$ be derived $I$-complete on $\mathcal D$. For each generator $a_i$ of Step 2, Step 3 gives $T(N,a_i)=0$. Represent $N$ by the K-injective $J$ of Step 1. Apply [lem-sp-levelwise-kinjective-tower-image] with $G=u_*$ and $X=X(J,a_i)$. It identifies $Ru_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}X$ with the actual multiplication tower on $u_*J$, a representative of $Ru_*N$: constant-$A$ direct image is $A$-linear, so $u_*(a_i)=a_i$ on that complex. The canonical comparison of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] now gives
$$T(Ru_*N,a_i)\cong Ru_*T(N,a_i)=0.$$
Step 3 gives vanishing of the localized derived internal Hom for each $a_i$ on every slice of $\mathcal C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-complete-elements-ideal], the sections with that vanishing form a sheaf of ideals. It contains all the generators and therefore every local section of $I\underline A$, since this ideal sheaf is locally generated by the $a_i$. Thus $Ru_*N$ is derived $I$-complete. No finite-quotient projection formula or perfectness assumption is used.

source.place: Tag 099J, lemma-pushforward-derived-complete, preservation assertion; multiplication-tower proof via Tag 0997 and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim

proof.text:
Write $F=Lu^*$, $G=Ru_*$, and $C=C_{\mathcal D}$. For $M\in D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal C,A)$ and $N\in D_{\mathrm{comp}}(\mathcal D,A)$, Step 2 and then Step 1 give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(CFM,N)\xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto h\eta_{FM}\ }\operatorname{Hom}(FM,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(M,GN).$$
Both bijections are natural. Step 4 makes $GN$ an object of the source complete category; since both complete categories are full subcategories, these are their actual Hom sets. The composite is the required adjunction $CF\dashv G$ on complete objects.

Let $\alpha:\mathrm{id}\to GF$ and $\beta:FG\to\mathrm{id}$ be the unit and counit of Step 1, and let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to C$ be the completion unit of Step 2. The new unit at $M$ is
$$M\xrightarrow{\alpha_M}GFM\xrightarrow{G\eta_{FM}}GCFM.$$
It is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{CFM}$ under the composite bijection of Step 5. The new counit at a complete $N$ is the unique map $e_N:CFGN\to N$ with
$$e_N\eta_{FGN}=\beta_N;$$
existence and uniqueness are the reflector bijection. It is the inverse image of $\mathrm{id}_{GN}$ under Step 5. Naturality of $\alpha$ and $\eta$ gives naturality of the new unit. For a map $t:N\to N'$ of complete objects, precomposing both $t e_N$ and $e_{N'}CFG(t)$ with $\eta_{FGN}$ gives $t\beta_N=\beta_{N'}FG(t)$; uniqueness in the reflector bijection gives their equality. Finally the two triangle identities are the inverse-bijection identities of Step 5 applied to identity maps. Thus this is precisely the adjunction normalized by the two specified Hom bijections.
